newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysians also attacked ringgit - Mahathir.
newsitem.headline: Malaysians also attacked ringgit - Mahathir.

text.p: Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad believes Malaysians were also involved in the recent speculative attacks on the ringgit, newspapers said on Wednesday.
Malaysians became involved by making the local currency available to speculators and may also have been looking to make profit for themselves, he was quoted as saying on Tuesday.
"I do not know if it is banks...but someone (local) is making available the (ringgit) currency," he told reporters on the northern island of Langkawi.
"There is also evidence that some locals are taking advantage of the situation to make profit.
"We hope they do not get involved in this...because it is damaging our economy," he said.
Mahathir has blamed U.S. financier George Soros for an attack on Southeast Asian currencies over the past month that has forced de facto devaluations of the Thai baht and the Philippine peso.
Indonesia widened the trading band for the rupiah and the tough Singapore dollar also fell sharply. The ringgit slipped to a 38-month low of 2.65 to the dollar.

"The government has definite evidence that the pressure on the ringgit and other ASEAN currencies was caused by George Soros," Mahathir said. "But, we cannot disclose the evidence now. There is no doubt that he did it..."
